facts.raw_span: A 52-year-old woman
history of long-standing diplopia
persistent vertical misalignment
anomalous band in the right orbit
surgically excised without improvement in motility
diplopia remained stable in primary gaze
orthotropic in primary position
elevation deficit of the right eye
The globes were unremarkable with no measured proptosis
retroocular fat, optic nerves and sheaths, optic chiasm, and brain parenchyma appeared normal
right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion
it was unchanged from the previous study

concepts.why: The presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle, with enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle, suggests orbital myositis.
The elevation deficit of the right eye and the presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion are consistent with thyroid-associated orbitopathy.
The presence of an anomalous band in the right orbit and a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion suggests orbital fibrosis.
The history of long-standing diplopia and the elevation deficit of the right eye are consistent with superior oblique myokymia.
The history of long-standing diplopia and the elevation deficit of the right eye are consistent with Brown syndrome.
The presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion and the history of an anomalous band in the right orbit suggest orbital inflammatory disease.
The elevation deficit of the right eye and the presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion are consistent with extraocular muscle restriction.
The presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion suggests an orbital tumor.
The elevation deficit of the right eye and the presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion are consistent with dysthyroid orbitopathy.
The presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion and the history of an anomalous band in the right orbit suggest orbital pseudotumor.

rationales.F04: The presence of an anomalous band in the right orbit suggests a possible orbital fibrosis or orbital tumor, but the lack of improvement after surgical excision makes orbital myositis less likely.
rationales.F05: The absence of improvement in motility after surgical excision of the anomalous band suggests that the underlying cause of the diplopia may not be related to orbital myositis or thyroid-associated orbitopathy.
rationales.F11: The presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion with signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle suggests a possible orbital fibrosis or extraocular muscle restriction.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of long-standing diplopia, persistent vertical misalignment, and elevation deficit of the right eye, combined with the presence of an anomalous band in the right orbit and a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion, support the diagnosis of Extraocular Muscle Restriction, which is further strengthened by the lack of improvement in motility after surgical excision of the anomalous band.
